text:
anya: Heads up — in the python sample app I just hit a redaction hole. When REDWOOD_LOG_LEVEL=debug the requests transport logs headers before our redaction hook runs, so Authorization shows up in stdout. Repro in 0.9.2.

chris: I can repro. looks like order-of-ops bug in the transport middleware. quick repro:```python\n# sample_app/main.py (simplified)\nimport os\nfrom redwood import RedwoodClient\nclient = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))\nresp = client.completions.create(prompt='hi')\n```\nrun with `REDWOOD_LOG_LEVEL=debug python sample_app/main.py` and you'll see a line like `DEBUG:requests.packages.urllib3.connectionpool:Sending headers: {'Authorization': 'Bearer ...'}`

sam: temporary workaround: set REDWOOD_LOG_LEVEL=info in CI and locally until we patch. also you can explicitly set REDWOOD_REDACT_HEADERS to `authorization,cookie` — but that only helps if redaction runs before logging.

leo: filing a small change to the python SDK to ensure redact middleware runs earlier in the call path. PR incoming. Also noticed a related OTEL quirk: when sampling rate <1.0 some spans don't get request_id added by our otel hook in the JS SDK sample app. Might be two separate ordering issues.

anya: For the JS sample (nextjs) I saw that fetch wrapper doesn't forward traceparent if we rely on next's built-in fetch wrapper. Minimal repro: in /app/route.ts `fetch('/api/llm')` -> server handler then calls Redwood SDK; the outgoing request lacks traceparent header. Works if I use globalThis.fetch directly.

chris: sounds like the otel instrumentation wrapper isn't patching next's runtime fetch. We should add a test in sample-apps that runs in dev mode + patched fetch. Test idea: instrumented request adds `x-request-id` and `traceparent`, assert presence in e2e logs.

leo: I'll add a unit test for python that flips log order and a JS e2e for fetch/traceparent. Devex-bot — can you add a flaky label to the existing telemetry CI job until the fixes land?

devex-bot: telemetry-ci job updated: +flaky label applied to job "telemetry-integration" (see https://ci.internal/telemetry/4821).

sam: QA checklist for the fixes: 1) REDWOOD_LOG_LEVEL=debug should never show Authorization or cookie values in stdout. 2) `x-request-id` should appear on every outgoing request (even when sampling drops spans). 3) traceparent must be forwarded when using Next.js runtime fetch. 4) Update sample-apps README with how to set REDWOOD_REDACT_HEADERS and how to run e2e.

anya: thanks — assigning followups: leo will open python PR, chris will add JS e2e, sam will add README notes and a short blurb in onboarding that warns about dev debug logs. I'll paste the failing log here if anyone wants to triage further. :thumbsup:
